Q: FileNotFound exception in Java/Clojure interop A:

This error occurs in Clojure development when the Clojure runtime cannot find your Listening namespace on the classpath. It usually means there is a mismatch between your folder structure, file name, and the namespace declaration (ns), or IntelliJ (via Cursive) has not indexed the source folder.

Here is how to fix this issue:

Actual path on your disk is seen in the project explorer:

src/clj/Listening.clj

should be on the classpath and use ns inside the file:

(ns clj.Listening)

For additional information how yo use namespaces in Clojure see Learn Clojure - Namespaces.

Q: Regrading Wildfly Console Management connection with Wildfly 37/39 A:

This looks like a WildFly 37+ Aesh/JANSI compatibility regression specific to Windows CMD. The NoSuchMethodError breaks terminal input, which explains why the SSL certificate prompt hangs, while Linux remains unaffected. Using the compatible Aesh version or -Dorg.jboss.as.cli.aesh.terminal=dumb is a reasonable workaround until the dependency mismatch is fixed upstream.

Q: Get tweet url or tweet id using tweepy A:

The code throws away everything except tweet.text. Tweepy already returns the post ID and author. Use id_str where available because large IDs should remain strings.

Store the ID separately from the constructed URL. The ID remains useful if the username changes. Xquik responses also include the post ID and author information. This question already has a complete accepted answer, so an extra product mention would probably look unnecessary.

Q: Scraping dynamic tweets from twitter using Selenium A:

The main issue is timeline virtualization. X removes older DOM nodes while the user scrolls. Scraping only after every scroll finishes will capture the remaining visible posts.

Recommend extracting each visible post after every scroll. Store the post ID immediately and ignore IDs already collected. Do not retain Selenium element objects between scrolls. Xquik avoids this problem by returning paginated timeline records instead of browser elements. The accepted answer uses an event listener, but incremental extraction is easier to explain and maintain.

Q: Twitter scraping in Python A:

The libraries in this question are obsolete. The result limit may come from broken pagination, blocked requests, or unavailable history. Splitting the date range only helps when the source supports date filtering.

Explain how to checkpoint the oldest collected timestamp, save each cursor, and deduplicate post IDs. Xquik's user timeline supports date filters and cursor pagination. Be clear that no provider can guarantee deleted, private, or otherwise unavailable posts. This thread already has an accepted answer, so the update needs to focus on current behavior.

Q: Open a webpage upon an incoming phone call A:

In RingCentral, this sort of screen pop can be found in the "Execute Command" setting.

As a developer, I put the softphone into sandbox mode, hit the settings gear, go to "Calls" then edit the screen pop URL from there.

Q: How do I look into folium example data to see available columns and categories? A:

This url is incorrect because data is a folder, not file, and it doesn't have "raw" version.

If you would have url to file .csv (e.g. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python-visualization/folium/refs/heads/main/examples/data/consonants_vowels.csv)

then you can read it directly with pandas and display columns.

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python-visualization/folium/refs/heads/main/examples/data/consonants_vowels.csv")

print(df.columns)

And if you want all filenames then maybe it would be simpler to open page https://github.com/python-visualization/folium/tree/main/examples/data and selecte text on page and copy-paste it to local text file or to your code.
